content: ACP1, also known as low molecular weight protein tyrosine phosphatase, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the ACP1 gene. The protein product of this gene is a member of the phosphotyrosine protein phosphatase family. It exhibits enzymatic activity as both an acid phosphatase and a protein tyrosine phosphatase. Specifically, it catalyzes the hydrolysis of protein tyrosine phosphate into protein tyrosine and orthophosphate. Additionally, this enzyme is capable of hydrolyzing orthophosphoric monoesters into alcohol and orthophosphate. The ACP1 gene is genetically polymorphic, meaning it exists in multiple genetic forms. There are three common alleles at the corresponding genetic locus, which result in six distinct phenotypes. Each allele appears to encode at least two electrophoretically distinct isoenzymes, referred to as Bf and Bs, which are produced in allele-specific ratios. Furthermore, three transcript variants encoding distinct isoforms of the enzyme have been identified for this gene. In terms of protein interactions, ACP1 has been demonstrated to interact with EPH receptor A2 and EPH receptor B1, which are members of the ephrin receptor family involved in various cellular processes.
